AT.name: Weisser Salbei
AT.citation: Species-specific German name for Salvia apiana across many independent German-language retailers (herbathek.com, jani-online.de, wurzelsepp.de, evi-gampl.de); shared DACH-region commercial vocabulary, no Austria-specific variant found

CH.name: Weisser Salbei
CH.citation: Same shared German-language commercial name as DE/AT; no Switzerland-specific variant found

DE.name: Weisser Salbei
DE.citation: Consistent species-specific name across many independent German retailers (herbathek.com, jani-online.de, Kraeuterhaus Wurzelsepp, evi-gampl.de, Waldglueck), always given alongside the binomial Salvia apiana

ES.name: Salvia blanca
ES.citation: Consistent species-specific name across independent Spanish retailers (Bazar Al Andalus, Casaquesuma, EcoMagic, Promesse de Fleurs ES); one source explicitly distinguishes it from Salvia officinalis

FR.name: Sauge blanche
FR.citation: Cross-confirmed species-specific French name (Bazar Al Andalus vernacular listing; consistent with the species' Wikipedia-linked vernacular name record)

GB.name: White sage
GB.citation: UK retailers (speedyseeds.co.uk, UK-based Etsy sellers) explicitly identify "White Sage" as Salvia apiana by binomial, distinguishing it from the Artemisia ludoviciana ambiguity documented elsewhere in North American retail

MX.name: Salvia blanca
MX.citation: Wilken-Robertson, M. (2020), Etnobotanica Kumiai: El Conocimiento Sobre Las Plantas Nativas de Un Pueblo Indigena de Baja California; documented Indigenous Kumiai/Paipai usage, not merely retail terminology

US.name: White sage
US.citation: U.S. Fish & Wildlife Service, species profile, Salvia apiana
